notes: counted = model's share of the expected two-way votes already counted (timeline); map f = share of the municipality's polling sections received.
Count path rebuilt from each section's TSE receipt time (DT_BU_RECEBIDO + 3 h = UTC), not from the results site's publication times.

stats.settle = first time after which P (model) or the price (market) stayed >= 0.9 on the eventual winner to the end (the registered definition, night.evaluate); it can fall before 1% is counted when the prior alone already gives P >= 0.9.
Solid model lines and the headline statistics are v1. Dashed v2 lines are a sensitivity whose settings were chosen after the result was known, using only earlier elections; map projections remain v1.
Prior: 2022 first round by municipality, same two candidates.

stats.settle_gated: model = max(registered model settle, gate), gate = first minute with >= 1% counted in that race; lead = minutes from the model's gated settle to lead_vs settling (positive: model first).

Sensitivity (v3, poll start): the same model as v1, started from the last two weeks of polls instead of the previous election alone. The 24 polls that ended 2022-10-16 to 2022-10-29 put Lula at 52.1% of the Lula + Bolsonaro vote (the prior had 52.9%); the swing is allowed an error of 5.7 points, the root-mean-square error of the same kind of poll average in 5 earlier elections of this country. The official result was 50.9%. The chance exists from poll close, before any count, and fades into the count as counted votes take over. It was designed after the result was known, so it is a sensitivity, not a forecast; v1 stays the headline.

sensitivities.label: tau mixture over earlier nights (chosen after the result was known)
sensitivities.note: An equal-weight mixture over the reporting-order errors that 3 earlier count nights needed (mx2012 0.015, mx2018 0.02, br2022r1 0). Same point forecast as the base model (rho 0.8, kappa 50,000); only the band and the win chance allow for those 3 different errors instead of one. Built from earlier nights only, but chosen after this result was known, so it is a sensitivity, not a forecast.

sensitivities.label: v3: poll start (chosen after the result was known)
sensitivities.note: The same model as v1, started from the final polls: the national swing begins at the average of 24 polls from the last 14 days (Wikipedia poll tables; Lula 52.1% of the Lula + Bolsonaro vote against 52.9% in the prior) with a sd of 5.7 points, the root-mean-square error of the same kind of poll average in 5 earlier elections. The reporting-order error enters as counted votes take over, so the chance exists from poll close, before any count, and fades into the count. Nothing from this night's count, prices or exit polls is an input, but it was designed after the result was known: a sensitivity, not a forecast.
